The team was led by third-year head coach [[Avery Johnson]] and played its home games at [[Coleman Coliseum]] in [[Tuscaloosa, Alabama]] as a member of the [[Southeastern Conference]]. They finished the season 20–16, 8–10 in SEC play to finish in a tie for ninth place. They defeated [[2017–18 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] and [[2017–18 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]] in the [[2018 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] before losing in the semifinals to [[2017–18 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they defeated [[2017–18 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]] in the First Round before losing in the Second Round to [[2017–18 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]]. ==Previous season== The [[2016–17 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Crimson Tide]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 19–15 overall and 8–10 in [[2016–17 SEC men's basketball season|SEC play]] to finish in a tie for fifth place. They defeated [[2016–17 Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball team|Mississippi State]] and [[2016–17 South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball team|South Carolina]] to advance to the semifinals of the [[2017 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] where they lost to [[2016–17 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]]. On November 25, 2017, Alabama participated in one of the strangest moments of NCAA basketball history. During their game against #14 ranked [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota Golden Gophers]], Alabama's bench players left the bench area during a scuffle with Minnesota's players midway through the second half, which resulted in Alabama's entire bench being ejected. Not long after the ejections, Dazon Ingram fouled out with 11:37 left in the game, which resulted in Alabama playing the rest of the game in a 4 vs. 5 manner. Not long afterwards, John Petty turned his ankle and could not return for the rest of the game, thus leaving Alabama with only three players with 10:41 left in the contest. From that point on Alabama was forced to play with only senior shooting guard/small forward Riley Norris, freshman power forward Galin Smith, and star freshman point guard [[Collin Sexton]] in a 3-on-5 setting throughout the rest of the game. While Minnesota was up by as many as 15 points during the undermanned portion of the game, Alabama would fight to cut the deficit to as few as 3 points due to Collin Sexton's leadership, which included a 40 point game from him. However, the Golden Gophers would ultimately hold on to win 89–84 over the shorthanded Crimson Tide. Despite losing, Alabama would improve their rank to #24 due to their performance while undermanned and nearly upsetting Minnesota that night. The game would be described as one of the strangest in college basketball history.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986392 |title=Alabama, down to 3 players
